card.title: Steam Deck - dump/modify controller board firmware

source.title: Steam Deck - dump/modify controller board firmware

symptoms: need to back up or edit controller firmware
lost serial data after MCU swap

claims.statement: The Steam Deck controller MCU (Renesas RA4E1) firmware can be dumped in USB boot mode with SteamOS's rfp-cli (or the steamdeck-controller-collect tool); bootloader first, application at 0x00008000–0x00040000, calibration/provisioning incl. both serial numbers at 0x08000000–0x08002000.
Edited regions need a recalculated CRC-32 (IEEE, little endian) with an extra final XOR; the serial block CRC covers 0x08000004–0x080000FF and is stored in the first 4 bytes at 0x08000000.
Without serials the Deck still runs, but automatic firmware/BIOS updates may not.

procedure: Put the MCU in USB boot mode (MD to ground).
Dump with rfp-cli or steamdeck-controller-collect; keep backups.
Edit in a hex editor; recompute region CRCs.
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Firmware modification can damage the controller board or Deck.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
